heard: We've been drawing the sun the wrong color our entire lives. For generations, children's drawings and even professional astronomers have classified our star as a yellow dwarf. But astronauts aboard the International Space Station observe a brilliant, blindingly white disk set against black space. Surprisingly, the sun's actual peak emission is in the green portion of the visible spectrum. Human eyes perceive this broad mixture of wavelengths as white because it stimulates all our color receptors simultaneously. This yellow star we see from Earth is actually an atmospheric illusion called Rayleigh scattering. Nitrogen and oxygen molecules deflect blue light away, leaving the remaining direct sunlight appearing yellow to our eyes. This stolen blue light paints our sky, while the leftover rays make us believe our white star is golden.
